A NOTE FROM THE FOUNDER

Muhammad Zuhair Zeb

Sometimes, the opportunities we cannot find become the opportunities we choose to create for others.
Read the founder's full message +

I did not begin with a clear plan for where I wanted to go. I began by exploring, learning new skills, and trying things for myself. Over time, those experiences shaped not only the work I wanted to do, but also the kind of impact I wanted to make.

I was born in Abbottabad, and my roots are in Swabi, Pakistan. Today, I study Artificial Intelligence at Islamia College University Peshawar. My path into technology started with curiosity. During the COVID period, I taught myself graphic design and video editing, then started a YouTube channel. Reaching 1,000 subscribers felt like a big achievement. Losing the channel after a deal went wrong was a hard lesson, but it also gave me a reason to start again.

That time, I chose WordPress.

What began as learning a new skill grew into freelance work, real clients, and more than four years of experience building websites. I also tried running my own eCommerce business. I eventually closed it, but the experience taught me lessons about business, responsibility, and the difference between having an idea and making it work.

Not every attempt worked out the way I hoped. Yet each one taught me something useful. I learned that progress does not always come from getting things right the first time. Sometimes, it comes from being willing to start again with what you have learned.

As I continued learning and working, I also had the chance to help other students develop practical skills. That experience changed how I thought about education. I began to see that many students are willing to learn and have ideas worth exploring, but they do not always have the right space, guidance, or team to put those ideas into practice.

I understood that feeling. Learning a skill had opened doors for me, but it was the chance to use that skill, work on real projects, and learn through experience that helped me move forward.

I started asking myself a simple question: What if more students had a place where they could learn by doing, work together, and build something before they even graduated?

That question led me to start Sociapi Society in December 2025 at Islamia College University Peshawar.

I wanted to create more than another student society. I wanted to build a community where students could explore technology and creativity, develop practical skills, share knowledge, and take their ideas beyond the classroom. A place where beginners could find their starting point, students could learn from one another, and people could gain experience by taking on real responsibilities.

Since then, Sociapi has grown through events, bootcamps, learning programs, and students contributing across universities. Every step has brought its own challenges, and there is still much to learn and improve. What matters most to me is not simply how many events we hold or how much the community grows. It is what students gain from being part of it.

A student who learns a new skill, a volunteer who gains the confidence to lead, or a team that turns an idea into a working project may seem like small steps on their own. Together, they are what make a community valuable.

I do not believe students should have to wait until they graduate to start doing meaningful work. They can learn, create, solve problems, and help others while they are still discovering their own path. They do not need to know everything before they begin. They need the willingness to learn, the courage to try, and the chance to put their knowledge to use.

That is the kind of environment I want Sociapi to build.

I am still learning myself. I am still exploring Artificial Intelligence, building with technology, and discovering better ways to turn ideas into useful work. Starting Sociapi has taught me that having an idea is only the beginning. Building something that lasts takes patience, teamwork, responsibility, and people who care enough to keep improving it.

Although I started Sociapi, I do not want its future to depend on one person. I want it to grow through the ideas, efforts, and contributions of the people who become part of it. I hope future members will take what we build today, improve it, and create opportunities that reach students we may never meet ourselves.

When I look back, I do not see a perfect journey. I see things I tried, lessons I learned, mistakes I made, and moments when I had to begin again. Those experiences have taught me that you do not need to have your entire future figured out to take a meaningful first step.

You can start with one skill, one idea, or one small effort. What matters is what you choose to do with it.

My hope is that Sociapi helps students discover what they are capable of, gain the confidence to act on their ideas, and learn to create opportunities rather than wait for them. And when they have the chance to move forward, I hope they will help someone else do the same.

Because to me, the real success of Sociapi will not be measured only by what we build as a society, but also by what the people who grow here go on to build themselves.

Thank you to every student, volunteer, mentor, and supporter who has been part of this journey. We are still growing, still learning, and still building. I look forward to what we can create together.
